correctness.rationale: The known Eğecioğlu–Remmel multipartite multivariate degree enumerator identifies degree−1 counts with n−2 independent uniform assignments, with r−2 over all n sites and k−1 for each part over n−k permitted outside vertices. Absence of any occupation gives p=(1−1/n)^{r−2}(1−1/(n−k))^{(r−1)(k−1)}, same-part two-site s and different-part two-site t exactly as RESULT.md, hence E[L]=np and Var(L)=np(1−p)+n(k−1)(s−p²)+n(n−k)(t−p²). All allowed draw pools have ≥n/2 sites, giving a uniform log Taylor error and σ²=e^(−1)−2e^(−2)>0 for Var(L)/n; E[L]=n/e+O(1) uniformly. For any fixed j distinct vertices, mixed Möbius differences of log joint empty events have size O_j(n^{1−|B|}); connected-hypergraph cancellation bounds joint cumulants O_j(n^{1−j}). Repeated labels contribute O_j(n^{1−d}) for d distinct underlying sites. Summing j-tuples yields κ_j(L)=O_j(n), hence normalized higher cumulants vanish and method of moments gives Gaussian convergence for arbitrary equal-part factorizations. Independently enumerated all labeled spanning trees of seven small (n,k) cases and matched exact rational moments; these finite tests do not establish the CLT.

originality.rationale: The 1994 Eğecioğlu–Remmel work already provides the full degree generating polynomial and marginal one-vertex leaf probability; finite exact moment identities are immediate consequences and are not credited as independently original. The assessed result is the uniform changing-part-count CLT and a positive universal total-leaf variance constant. The original full primary Section 6, including leaf probability, was examined; it did not state the claimed global uniform CLT. A broader modern occupancy CLT might imply this special consequence, which remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: A standard central limit theorem for independent nonidentical occupancy schemes could imply the uniform case without stating spanning trees.
The degree generating function from 1994 contains all finite marginal information, so novelty must be restricted to the uniform asymptotic analysis.

value.rationale: A universal Gaussian law for the natural number of leaves in random spanning trees across complete graphs, balanced complete bipartite graphs and intermediate regular multipartite hosts gives nontrivial distributional information beyond a known one-vertex mean. Uniform control across changing host geometry is a meaningful probabilistic refinement.

limitations: Equal-sized parts and uniform unweighted spanning tree; no unequal-part or weighted-tree extension.
Only scalar total-leaf CLT, not a joint degree profile theorem or Berry–Esseen rate.
